prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect are a discovery in the statutory sense: a new class of electronic matter, defined by band topology and spin-orbit coupling, with protected edge and surface states that nobody had anticipated before Kane and Mele's Z2 classification. The theory-plus-experiment structure is unusually clean, because Kane and Mele supply the decisive theory and Molenkamp's group delivers the first observation of edge transport in HgTe wells. The field has matured over fifteen years, with independent confirmation in many materials and probes, including ARPES on 3D materials, and it has changed how materials are searched for and understood. From my own work I can say that topology is now a standard organising principle in first-principles electronic-structure calculations, which is a good measure of lasting impact. Three of the four colleagues who ranked it placed it in the top three, so it is also the candidate on which opinion is most evenly spread.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal that directly led to Molenkamp's experiment, and Fu, Kane, Moore, Balents, Roy and Hasan were decisive for the 3D generalisation. A three-name prize drawn from the supplied list will therefore look incomplete to some, and the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter makes some colleagues wary of closeness. I take the 2016 overlap seriously but think it is manageable: that prize honoured topological phases and transitions in the integer quantum Hall and Haldane setting, whereas the Z2 classification and time-reversal-protected states are a distinct and later discovery. If the committee judges the attribution irreparable, optical lattice clocks are the best fallback.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B021 only eighth because Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are missing from the credited names, which weakens fairness, and because the topic sits close to the 2016 prize on topological phases.
responses.response: I agree that omitting Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real fairness problem and I will not pretend otherwise. But the credited trio still covers the decisive theoretical formulation of the Z2 state and the first experimental observation, and the statutes limit us to three people. The BHZ proposal was a material-specific prediction of an effect Kane and Mele had already conceived, which is why I treat the Kane-Mele concept as the primary theoretical credit. On the 2016 overlap, that prize concerned topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall class, not time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators. I would welcome an explicit citation wording that makes this distinction. Where I do share your caution is that this should not rest on my familiarity with the electronic-structure side of the field.

responses.point: Olsson ranked the aberration-corrected electron microscopy trio first, as a transformative instrument with overdue recognition, and ranked B021 second.
responses.response: I take the instrumentation case seriously and it is a materials-physics subject I know well, since much of the atomic-scale evidence for defects, interfaces and 2D materials depends on it. My reservation is the framing risk that you yourself note: the prize would honour an enabling instrument rather than a discovery about nature, and the TEM versus STEM corrector lineage leaves Krivanek and Dellby outside the credited list. I would still support it, and B011 is not among my alternatives only because of the two-slot limit. Topological insulators give us a new state of matter with an instrument-independent result, and since you also place it second, I hope we can agree that it is a strong common ground.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as a measurement-limited advance with an uncontested two-person credit, mature and with a stable interpretation.
responses.response: Of all the candidates, the clocks have the cleanest attribution, and I ranked them second for that reason. My difference is about the kind of discovery. The lattice clock is a decisive invention with outstanding precision, but it comes after the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and is, in part, an incremental advance within a field the committee has repeatedly honoured. A new class of matter is a larger conceptual step. I also think the redefinition of the second is a reason to wait slightly, not a reason to act now. If the committee prefers clean credit over breadth of conceptual impact, I would accept B052 without objection.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked B052 first and B021 third, noting missing names from the experimental path to 3D topological insulators and some overlap with the 2016 prize.
responses.response: The 3D omissions are fair, and I would frame the citation around the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant, where the three credited names are strongest, rather than claim the whole of the 3D story. On the 2016 point I disagree mildly, for the reason I gave to Mehlig. On clocks, I defer to you on the metrology details such as the priority among early lattice-clock proposals, which I cannot judge as well as you can.

uncertainties: Whether a prize limited to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp will be seen as unfair to Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and how the citation should be drawn to limit this.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize makes the committee regard B021 as a continuation rather than a distinct discovery.
Whether colleagues weigh the cleaner attribution and unanimous top-eight support of optical lattice clocks above the broader conceptual novelty of B021.
I recall the HgTe experimental history from memory and have not verified it independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I work in theoretical magnetism and electronic-structure theory, so topological materials are close to my own field, which may make me more enthusiastic about B021, but no personal or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or any other credited name is documented.
